name: St. Peter's Basilica
_about: ST PETER'S BASILICA AND SQUARE, Rome: Bernini's colonnade of four rows of Tuscan columns in two arms round the obelisk and the two fountains, the straight corridors to the front, the steps; Maderno's front in the giant order (eight columns) with its loggia, attic and thirteen statues, the nave, Michelangelo's Greek cross with its apses and the dome on its drum of paired columns, raised by Della Porta, its lantern 136.57 m to the cross. Written by tools/archgen/st_peters.py.

north colonnade._about: Bernini's colonnade: two arms of four rows of Tuscan columns, each arm on arcs round its own centre either side of the obelisk -- from those two points the four rows line up as one

north corridor._about: the straight corridors (Braccio di Costantino north, di Carlo Magno south) from the colonnade to the front

sagrato steps._about: the steps up from the piazza to the sagrato, the platform before the front

paul pedestal._about: the pedestals of Sts Peter and Paul at the foot of the steps

obelisk lions._about: ...the four bronze lions it stands on

obelisk crown._about: the bronze over it: the Chigi mounts and star (a cage of bars), the cross

Maderno fountain lower bowl._about: the great bowl turned up like a mushroom's cap, the water spilling over its rim...

Bernini fountain lower bowl._about: the great bowl turned up like a mushroom's cap, the water spilling over its rim...

paving._about: the piazza's paving: sampietrini, the little basalt setts of Rome (finish), over the oval and the piazza retta

ray 0._about: the travertine rays from the obelisk across the setts

ellipse band._about: the travertine band of the ellipse round the obelisk, inside the fountains

podium._about: the podium the basilica stands on, its floor three metres over the piazza

front._about: the front in the giant Corinthian order through the portals' storey and the loggia's, the Benediction loggia in the middle, the attic over the entablature; the narthex behind it

front columns._about: the 8 giant columns standing out of the order's pilasters

front entablature._about: the entablature breaking forward over the columns: architrave, frieze, the cornice standing out

front inscription._about: the dedication's band along the frieze

front pediment._about: the pediment over the middle 4 columns, before the attic

north clock._about: the clocks over the end bays, a dial in each arch

nave._about: the nave's east block: the nave and its aisles, Maderno's lengthening of Michelangelo's cross

nave chapels._about: ...its west block, wider by the great side chapels

clerestory._about: the nave's high wall over the aisles' terraces, its vault under the roof

cross._about: Michelangelo's Greek cross round the crossing: its corners standing out, chamfered to the apses; the giant Corinthian order, two rows of windows between its pilasters, the attic

cross roof._about: its flat roof, the terrace round the dome's base, the well over the crossing

north apse._about: the three apses, in the same order and attic: half rings on the cross's faces

north apse vault end._about: the vault's cut end over the cross's terrace, closed

dome base._about: the high round base over the terraces the drum stands on

dome._about: Michelangelo's drum: sixteen buttresses with a pair of Corinthian columns on each, a window between each two under triangular and segmental pediments by turns; the attic with its paired strips; Della Porta's raised dome with its sixteen DOUBLE ribs and three rows of lucarnes; the lantern of paired columns, its spire, the ball and the cross, standing on the dome where it narrows to them (drum-dome by name)

dome well._about: the church's space on up through the dome's base to the drum's

north cupola._about: the two minor cupolas (Vignola's) at the cross's front corners

north chapel cupola 0._about: the small cupolas over the nave's side chapels

balustrade plinths._about: the balustrades' plinths, every run on the building (neoclassical.Balusters: the preferred L2 balustrade)
